notes: Independently audited all ten discovery and six expansion candidates using current official journal, publisher/platform and repository pages. Every candidate has a complete replacement route and audit note. Search snippets and policy silence were not used to establish a zero fee.

Fifteen routes are verified_free on the evidence inspected; JMLR remains needs_verification because its explicit publication-fee exclusion does not separately establish submission fees. Fifteen free routes comprise fourteen peer-reviewed journals plus one separately labeled moderated arXiv route.

A journal-specific blanket no-author-fees statement was accepted as covering submission and ordinary publication. Platform policy was applied only where the journal's current site established its applicability. Unknown compulsory costs were not converted to none.

The audit covers ordinary journal routes and repository dissemination. It does not imply free attendance at conferences, optional conference presentation, research-computing expenses, guaranteed editorial eligibility or acceptance. No selective waiver or institutional agreement is needed for the fifteen verified monetary routes.

Preparation, page/length, software maturity, repository deposit, membership/registration and material article-eligibility conditions were inspected and recorded. AI policies vary and must be checked against the actual human-directed workflow. In particular, TMLR's current FAQ expects human-sourced ideas/results, JOSS disallows AI-mediated review conversations except translation, and EISEJ restricts AI assistance in writing.

No ACM 2026 subscription/free-publication assumption was made. ACM, IEEE and conference venues are not among these sixteen routes. The EISEJ linked flyer timed out, so this audit relies on accessible official homepage and author policies instead.
This is a fee-policy audit by an independent agent, not human scientific review, a promise that every manuscript type qualifies, or a legal interpretation of author agreements.
